newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes sharply higher on weather.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes sharply higher on weather.

text.p: KCBT wheat futures closed sharply higher on harsh weather in the spring wheat growing region with some concern expressed about cold weather in portions of the U.S. winter wheat growing areas, traders said.
"The big thrust in wheat is the weather condition in the Northern Plains," a trader said.

Dealers said there were three major concerns currently dominating the market, the lack of moisture in western Kansas, too much moisture in the northern U.S. Midwest and the drop in temperatures in Kansas.

Meteorologists said already low temperatures in Kansas may dip further later this week. "We are watching it, because if it gets any colder it could put some winter wheat in danger," said Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio.
KCBT traders said trading was relatively quiet after the first half hour of dealings with gains in CBOT corn and soybeans also mentioned as a supportive influence.
"Beans and corn also are helpful to the upside," a trader said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 10 to 13-1/2 cents higher, with May up 10 at $4.12 a bushel.

Commission house buying and light commercial buying was cited, the traders said. But gains were limited by sales from Lind Waldock of one million in July and E.D. and F. Man International sold one million bushels of May, traders said.
The May/July traded at 25-1/2 to 26-1/2 cents, premium May and July/September traded at three cents, premium September, traders said.
KCBT wheat futures volume was estimated at 33,690 contracts, below the 39,825 traded Friday.
